data.title: Market prediction: What Gift Nifty says for opening; Vaishali Parekh gives 3 stocks - HDFC Bank, Cochin Shipyard, Waaree
data.description:
New Delhi, Sept. 15 -- The key benchmark indices of the Indian stock market are expected to trade with a cautious bias today, with crude oil prices remaining the biggest near-term risk for domestic equities. Renewed U.S.-Iran military tensions and the latest escalation involving Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis have raised concerns over a broader regional conflict and potential disruptions to global energy and shipping routes. While GIFT Nifty futures are indicating a technical rebound from last week's lows, the macroeconomic pressure from higher oil prices amid an uncertain geopolitical backdrop is likely to keep investor sentiment guarded at higher levels.

Gift Nifty signals a gap-up start

The Gift Nifty live chart is trading above the previous spot Nifty close and its previous close. The index is trading over 100 points above the previous spot Nifty close and over 50 points above the previous close.

Vaishali Parekh, Vice President - Technical Research at Prabhudas Lilladher, has predicted a gap-up start or the Indian stock market. She said the Gift Nifty live chart is trading above the previous spot Nifty close and its own previous close by over 100 and 50 points, respectively.

Speaking on the outlook for the Nifty 50 today, Vaishali Parekh said the 50-stock index, after witnessing a weak start with a gap-down near the 23250 zone, recovered steadily as the day progressed and closed near the 23400 zone. With a cautious approach would need to sustain the 23200 level in the coming sessions.

"The Nifty 50 index would need a decisive move above the 23,800 zone to establish conviction and, thereafter, can expect further follow-through of the positive move, whereas, on the downside, the 23,000 zone would be the important near-term support," said Parekh.

On the outlook for the Bank Nifty today, Parekh said, the key benchmark index opened with a gap down opening near the 55700 zone but indicated a decent recovery to end the session in the green above the 56,600 zone to show a big positive candle on the daily chart, with the bias slightly turning optimistic and can anticipate a further rise in the coming days.

"The Bank Nifty index would have the important support near the 54,500 level, while on the upside, the 50-EMA at the 57,200 level shall be the important hurdle which needs to be breached decisively to establish conviction," said Parekh.

Regarding stocks to buy today, Vaishali Parekh recommended these three intraday stocks: Cochin Shipyard, HDFC Bank, and Waaree Energies.

data.title: MHA calls meeting after 3 Italian passengers bypassed immigration at Delhi airport: What we know
data.description:
New Delhi, Sept. 15 -- The Union ministry of home affairs (MHA) will hold an emergency meeting with senior officials on Tuesday after three Italian passengers allegedly bypassed a mandatory immigration at Delhi airport and boarded a flight to Germany. The incident reportedly took place on September 4.

According to a report by Hindustan Times, the passengers first travelled from Amritsar to Delhi and then boarded a Lufthansa flight to German city of Munich.

They arrived in Delhi from Amritsar on AI 1115 at 12.50 am on September 4 and departed for Munich at 1.45 am.

The meeting, to be held later today, will be chaired by Union home secretary Govind Mohan. It will also be attended by secretary and additional secretary of the civil aviation ministry, Intelligence Bureau director, secretary and additional secretary of the home ministry, Bureau of Immigration (BoI) commissioner, Air India Group head and Delhi airport CEO.

Earlier, a show-cause notice was issued to Air India on September 12 by the Union ministry of civil aviation (MoCA). The action came after concerns were raised by the MHA over the handling of the passengers by the airline.

The Hindustan Times report further mentioned that Air India was yet to respond to the notice by MoCA.

The lapse likely occurred at Amritsar airport as the three passengers had travelled to Delhi from there to board their flight out of India. They, though, did not complete immigration formalities at the Delhi airport before boarding the flight.

The passengers were issued two boarding passes at the Amritsar airport and were supposed to complete their immigration at Delhi airport but instead they were directed to the international-to-international transfer. This allowed them to board the international flight without completing the mandatory process.

Amritsar is one of the airports where the Union government has introduced "hub-and-spoke model". According to this model, passengers travelling to international destinations can complete immigration formalities at the origin airport and then transferred to the international flight at the designated hub.

Passengers are only required to undergo security checks before boarding their international flights. However, in the present case, as the flights were not operating under hub-and-spoke arrangement, the passengers were required to undergo immigration formalities in Delhi. data.title: GSK strikes up to $750 million deal for cancer-targeting drug
data.description:
GSK said on Tuesday it had agreed a deal worth up to $750 million to buy a trispecific T cell-engager (TCE), a drug designed to help T-cells target cancer, from China-based biotechnology firm Chimagen Biosciences.

  • A trispecific T cell-engager is an engineered protein that brings T cells and tumor cells together while blocking immune checkpoints, enhancing cancer-killing ability with reduced off-target effects.

  • GSK will pay an upfront fee to acquire full global rights to the TCE program, and Chimagen will be eligible for development and commercial milestone-linked payments.

  • The London-listed company plans to develop and commercialize the drug for multiple myeloma, a type of blood cancer, with phase 1 trials expected to begin in 2027.

  • The deal marks the latest step in an oncology building spree under new CEO Luke Miels, who has vowed to expand GSK's cancer franchise ahead of looming patent losses on its top-selling HIV medicines.

  • Earlier this year, GSK bought lung cancer specialist Nuvalent for a $10.6 billion, its biggest acquisition in more than a decade.

  • In 2024, GSK bought rights to develop and sell an from Chimagen in an up to $850 million deal.

  • In October 2025, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved GSK's blood cancer drug Blenrep in a combination regimen, allowing it to return to the market nearly three years after it was withdrawn.

This information is subject to the disclosure requirements in Article 19 of Regulation (EU) 596/2014 (the EU Market Abuse Regulation) and section 5-12 of the Norwegian Securities Trading Act.

About Circio

Building circular RNA expression systems for enhanced gene and cell therapies

Circio Holding ASA is a biotechnology company developing novel circular RNA expression technology for gene and cell therapy.

Circio has established a unique circular RNA (circRNA) vector expression technology for next generation RNA, DNA and viral therapeutics. The proprietary circVec platform is based on a modular genetic construct designed for efficient biogenesis of multifunctional circRNA inside target cells. The circVec platform has applications in multiple therapeutic settings, including genetic medicine, cell therapy and chronic disease. It has demonstrated 75-fold increased RNA half-life and up to 60-fold enhanced protein expression vs. conventional mRNA-based viral and non-viral vector systems, with the potential to become a new gold-standard gene expression technology. The circVec R&D activities are being conducted by the wholly owned subsidiary Circio AB in Stockholm, Sweden.

data.title: South Korean shares end lower as rising bond yields weigh
data.description:
Key points:
  • KOSPI falls, foreigners net sellers
  • Korean won weakens against dollar
  • South Korea benchmark bond yield rises
  • For the midday report, please clicknL1N457013

Round-up of South Korean financial markets:

** South Korean shares closed lower after a session of volatile trade on Tuesday, as investors remained wary of rising bond yields.

** The benchmark KOSPI fell 57.12 points, or 0.85%, to 6,627.26, extending losses to a fourth consecutive session and posting the lowest close since September 3.

** The index swung between a gain of 0.5% and a loss of 1.5% during the session. It opened lower following Wall Street's overnight declines, briefly turned positive as chipmakers rebounded, and then fell back near the close.

** "Dip buying weakened on additional increases in bond yields and oil prices. The market is more sensitive to negative market movers than positive ones amid prevalent worries about a rate hike at the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy meeting later this week," said Lee Kyoung-min, an analyst at Daishin Securities.

** South Korean Finance Minister Nominee Lee Hyoung-il said at a parliamentary hearing that authorities would closely monitor the bond market and take market-stabilising measures if needed.

** Chipmaker Samsung Electronics fell 0.20% and peer SK Hynix lost 0.41%.

** Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution climbed 3.98%, while Hyundai Motor and sister automaker Kia Corp were down 1.21% and 1.93%, respectively.

** Steelmaker POSCO Holdings added 1.84%, while drugmaker Samsung BioLogics fell 0.56%.

** Of the total 917 traded issues, 254 shares advanced, while 623 declined.

** Foreigners were net sellers of shares worth 1.6 trillion won ($1.18 billion).

** The won was quoted at 1,359.4 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform , 0.97% lower than its previous close at 1,346.2.

** The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) rose by 6.5 basis points to 4.080%, hitting the highest level since October 2023, while the benchmark 10-year yield rose by 5.8 basis points to 4.590%, its highest since October 2022.

data.title: GSK to Buy Antibody Treatment From Chimagen for Up to $750 Million
data.description:
By Adam Whittaker

GSK said it agreed to buy an early-stage antibody-based treatment from biotechnology company Chimagen Biosciences in a deal valued at up to $750 million.

The London-listed pharmaceutical company said Tuesday that it would acquire Chimagen's trispecific T-cell engager (TCE) treatment and plans to develop it to treat the blood cancer multiple myeloma.

Multiple myeloma is generally considered treatable but isn't currently curable. Other TCE drugs have helped transform treatment but have difficult tolerability profiles, GSK said.

Chimagen's TCE is designed to improve tolerability and efficacy by binding to T-cells while also targeting two tumor-associated antigens, the company said. GSK hopes this will help drive wider adoption and earlier use in multiple myeloma treatment.

GSK will pay an upfront fee to acquire full global rights to the TCE program, and plans to advance the TCE into Phase 1 trials in 2027.

Chimagen will also receive success-based development and commercial milestone payments, GSK said.

Write to Adam Whittaker at adam.whittaker@wsj.com

The harmonised inflation rate in the bloc's second-biggest economy — adjusted for comparison with other euro zone countries — accelerated in August compared with the July reading of 2.4% and was at its highest level since May.

data.title: Uno Minda to invest ₹1,415 crore in capex across India
data.description:
Major auto components manufacturer, Uno Minda, on Tuesday announced a series of strategic capacity expansion and plant consolidation projects across its key business verticals with a combined investment of around ₹1,415 crore.

The investment would strengthen its manufacturing footprint, boost capacities across key divisions, and cater to surging demand from leading original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), the company said.

“These projects mark another significant step forward in Uno Minda’s long-term growth journey. Each of them is anchored in a clear and consistent principle — investing backed by orders or firm demand visibility, staying close to our customers, and building state of art manufacturing capabilities that are scalable, efficient and future-ready,” Ravi Mehra, Managing Director, Uno Mind, said.

The first project of the expansions includes a greenfield aluminium casting facility at Hosur (Tamil Nadu) with a capex of ₹510 crore. Uno Minda’s Aluminium Casting Division, which manufactures castings parts two-wheeler (2W), four-wheeler (4W) and commercial vehicles (CVs) — both ICE and EV — continues to see strong demand from OEMs, particularly in South India, it said.

With the existing Hosur facility at current location having reached its practical expansion limits, the company will establish a new greenfield facility on its another existing land parcel at Thally Road, Hosur, to create a scalable, future-ready manufacturing base for committed volumes and emerging business opportunities.

With this, the aluminium casting capacity at the Hosur location will be enhanced from around 13,000 MT to 34,000 MT at peak, and it will be implemented in a phased manner over the next three years, with Phase 1 expected to commence production by Q4FY28.

Uno Minda also said the Board of Directors has approved setting up a 3.3 million-unit 2W alloy wheel capacity plant at Kharkhoda, Haryana. This initiative includes the strategic relocation of two-million units of existing capacity from Supa, Maharashtra, to the Kharkhoda plant with an additional capex of ₹155 crore.

This will also be implemented in a phased manner over the next two years, with Phase 1 expected to commence production by Q4FY28

The company said its Board has also approved the expansion of moulding facility in Bengaluru, under its subsidiary Uno Minda Kyoraku, to cater to increased demand. The estimated capex for the expansion is around ₹80 crore and it is expected to commence operations by Q1FY28.

The company’s joint venture with Toyoda Gosei, Japan under Toyoda Gosei South India Private Limited will set up a new plant at CSN, Maharashtra, to manufacture interior and exterior automotive parts, airbags, hoses, and body sealing parts, it said.

“This will be the company’s third plant in India, following its first plant at Bidadi, Karnataka, and its second plant at Harohalli, Karnataka. The project is backed by new orders from customers. The estimated capex for this new plant is around ₹670 crore. The facility is expected to commence operations by Q4FY29,” the company added.

data.title: ZAWYA: Oman: O-Green installs landmark wind turbine in Duqm
data.description:
By Staff Writer

MUSCAT: Omani state-backed integrated clean energy platform O-Green has installed a 9.6 MW wind turbine at the Special Economic Zone at Duqm (SEZAD), describing it as the world’s largest onshore wind turbine installed outside mainland China.

The turbine, featuring blades nearly 100 metres long and a 115-metre tower, will supply renewable electricity to Duqm’s expanding industrial ecosystem, including the nearby Mawarid wind turbine manufacturing facility, according to O-Green.

Located near the OQ8 refinery, the turbine forms part of the Duqm City Renewable Energy initiative being developed through Naqaa Sustainable Energy, an O-Green subsidiary.

“For us, this turbine represents more than 9.6 MW of renewable generation. It represents the next stage of Oman’s energy transition: building renewable energy infrastructure while localising the technology and industrial capability behind it,” O-Green said.

Omani contractors and specialists participated across the project, including engineering, site works, construction and the complex transportation and installation of tower sections and blades. The turbine platform has also been engineered for the demanding operating conditions of the GCC, O-Green said.

The installation represents the single-turbine Duqm North component of the wider Duqm North and South Wind Project. Together, the two developments will comprise six turbines with combined capacity of 58 MW. Duqm South will account for the remaining five turbines and 48 MW.

Once operational, the wind projects are expected to generate around 190 GWh of electricity annually, supporting efforts to decarbonise industrial activity at the Special Economic Zone at Duqm and strengthen Oman’s emerging renewable-energy manufacturing ecosystem.

Futures on the CAC (FCEc1) and FTSE are also a touch softer, while DAX futures are unchanged.

Tech stocks could also be in focus for a second day after industry leaders called for a slowdown in AI development.

Europe's banks are also a sector to watch at the open after Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan said on Monday that he expects investment banking fees to drop by at least 10% in the third quarter.

data.title: Rentomojo IPO: Allotment today; check status online | 72.88x subscription - GMP signals 39% listing gains
data.description:
New Delhi, Sept. 15 -- Rentomojo IPO allotment is all set to be finalised today, 15 September. The mainboard IPO opened for bidding on 9 September and closed on 11 September.

The IPO received a strong response from investors, with the issue being subscribed 72.88 times on the third and final day of bidding. Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs) led the demand, with their portion subscribed 177.29 times, while the Non-Institutional Investors (NIIs) category was subscribed 67.93 times. The Retail Individual Investors (RIIs) portion also saw healthy interest, receiving 15.59 times subscription.

The shares of Rentomojo IPO is commanding a strong premium in the grey market ahead of allotment. The GMP of Rentomojo IPO is Rs.158, according to Investorgain.

The estimated listing price of Rentomojo IPO is likely to be Rs.562, which is 39.11% higher than the IPO price of Rs.404.

The Rs.1,255.57 crore Rentomojo IPO set its price band at Rs.384- Rs.404 per equity share. The issue opened for subscription on September 9 and closed on September 11.

The public issue consists of a combination of a fresh issue and an offer for sale (OFS). The fresh issue comprises 37.15 lakh equity shares worth Rs.150 crore, while the OFS includes 2.73 crore shares valued at Rs.1,105.57 crore.

The allotment of Rentomojo IPO shares is expected to be finalised on September 15, after the bidding process concludes. The company's shares are proposed to be listed on both the NSE and BSE, with September 17, 2026, as the tentative listing date.

The IPO proceeds will be deployed for multiple corporate requirements. The company plans to use a portion of the funds to repay or prepay, either fully or partially, certain outstanding borrowings, including accrued interest. Some of the proceeds will also be used towards lease rentals and licence fees for its warehouses and experience stores, while the balance will be allocated towards general corporate purposes.

Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors Ltd. is the book-running lead manager for the IPO, while Kfin Technologies Ltd. is acting as the registrar to the issue.

Rentomojo is an India-based direct-to-consumer rental and subscription platform that provides customers with flexible access to furniture and appliances without the need to bear the upfront cost of ownership.

Applicants can check the Rentomojo IPO allotment status on the official websites of BSE, NSE and KFin Technologies, the registrar to the issue.

After the allotment is finalised, refunds for unsuccessful applicants are expected to be initiated on September 16, while shares allotted to successful investors are likely to be credited to their Demat accounts on the same day.
